text:
maya (Support): Hey team, incoming escalation from Acme about streaming responses getting much worse p95/p99 starting last night. They say TTFB isn't great but the bigger issue is long pauses between chunks — perceived as streaming 'lag'. They've provided a short repro and logs.

jonas (Runtime): Thanks, can you paste the repro curl and a sample log? Streaming vs non-streaming comparison would help (TTFB vs total time).

maya (Support): Sure — repro command they sent:

```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\\n  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-2b","input":"stream test\"}' \\\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```

They measured: non-streaming (single response) p95 ~220ms, streaming TTFB ~200ms but p95 chunk-gap ~1.2s and p99 ~4.8s for some requests. Before yesterday deploy chunk-gap p99 was ~300-400ms.

li (SRE): Do they sit behind a proxy or CDN? Middlebox buffering often causes chunking delays. Also need to know if they're using HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1.

maya (Support): Acme says they use a custom edge proxy (nginx) in front of their app which talks to our hosted API over TLS. They confirmed HTTP/1.1 to us.

jonas (Runtime): HTTP/1.1 + some proxies can buffer until they see a full chunk or connection flush. On our side, the runtime flush cadence changed in the recent batching commit (rollout yesterday) — we increased internal buffer to 16KB to reduce small writes. That may increase inter-chunk pauses for low-volume streams.

diego (ML): To be clear: model token generation is steady; this sounds like a network/IO flush problem not model compute. Model logs show consistent per-token latency.

ops-bot: Deploy 2026-03-12T23:14:12 by @jonas completed: runtime/batching-buffer-tune v3.4.1 -> v3.5.0

jonas (Runtime): ^ that deploy matches timing. We made an optimization to reduce syscall overhead by buffering up to 16KB before flush, but we added a dynamic flush threshold that should flush on end-of-sequence or explicit flush. Looks like some streaming paths didn't trigger explicit flush early enough.

li (SRE): Quick mitigation we can try: route a small percentage of traffic to pre-deploy runtime (v3.4.1) to confirm regression. Canary/rollback would prove cause.

maya (Support): Customer is on a paid plan and hitting production impact. They want a fast mitigation; can we push a config to lower flush buffer or enable aggressive flushing for streaming endpoints?

jonas (Runtime): Yes. There's a feature flag `stream.flush_threshold_bytes` currently default 16384. We can temporarily set to 512 or 0 (immediate flush) for hosted streaming endpoints. That should reduce chunk-gap at cost of more syscalls.

diego (ML): Also check if KV prefix cache introduced a short delay for the first chunk; but since TTFB is fine per their numbers, KV isn't root cause for chunk spacing.

li (SRE): I'll check Envoy/proxy settings. Envoy has `max_buffered_bytes` and `flush_interval` settings if it's being used in front. Some customer edge proxies also set `proxy_buffering on` in nginx which can stash chunks.

maya (Support): Acme also sent a raw tcpdump snippet showing pacing: they see bursts from our IP, then 4s quiet, then rest of stream. They suspect server side pacing.

jonas (Runtime): Please ask them to test direct curl from a host with no intermediate proxy to us (if OK security-wise). That isolates whether it's their edge buffering. Example test:

```
# from customer host with no proxy in path
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -o - | ts '%H:%M:%S'
```

(They may need to install `moreutils` for ts). If direct to us shows small chunk gaps, it's our side.

maya (Support): They ran the direct test. Results: same symptoms. So likely server-side.

jonas (Runtime): Ok urgent patch then. I'm going to push a temporary config toggle to reduce `stream.flush_threshold_bytes` to 512 for streaming routes and enable `force_immediate_flush=true` for the next hour for the impacted region.

li (SRE): I'll open a rule to route 10% of production to the previous runtime binary while we validate. If latency improves on the 10% path, we can roll the change.

sam (Billing): Heads up — if we change flush to immediate, token accounting should remain identical but clients will see more small chunks. No billing impact other than possibly more network egress requests. Just flagging so Support can brief customer.

maya (Support): Copy. I'll let Acme know we have a mitigation roll in progress and ask for their availability for a quick smoke test.

jonas (Runtime): Patch is staged. Roll command:

```
# platform-admin
redwoodctl config set /runtime/streams/flush_threshold_bytes 512 --scope=region-us-east-1 --reason=\"customer-impact: streaming chunk pause\"
redwoodctl config set /runtime/streams/force_immediate_flush true --scope=region-us-east-1
```

ops-bot: config change applied by @jonas at 2026-03-12T23:46:03

li (SRE): Also checking kernel-level TCP settings: `net.ipv4.tcp_low_latency` is off by default. In a few of our infra hosts we had `tcp_low_latency=1` for low-latency endpoints; not a universal setting. It's something to consider if we keep aggressive flushing.

diego (ML): After the patch we should run synthetic streaming load to measure p95/p99 chunk-gap and end-to-end quality. I can spin a small job that mimics their token pace.

maya (Support): Acme ran a quick smoke and reports immediate improvement: chunk gaps reduced to p95 ~320ms and p99 ~880ms. They still see occasional spikes but far better than before.

jonas (Runtime): Good. I'll keep the aggressive flush on for 2 hours and then revert to 2KB threshold while we implement a smarter adaptive flushing (flush on small idle periods + max delay). The longer term fix is to make flush behavior dependent on observed per-stream token rate.

li (SRE): Follow-up actions:
- Reproduce with synthetic load and measure p95/p99 (diego)
- Add unit/regression tests to ensure streaming flush hooks are invoked in all codepaths (jonas)
- Audit proxies for `proxy_buffering`/`max_buffered_bytes` defaults and document customer-facing guidance (maya + li)
- Plan a safe roll with perf guardrails (canary + fast rollback) (eng-sre)

sam (Billing): I'll prepare a short note for customer success incase Acme asks if any billing abnormalities occurred.

maya (Support): Thanks all — I'll update the thread with Acme's final verdict after a 24h observation window.

jonas (Runtime): One more note for engineers: if you search commit `b2f9c1` it's where the buffer increase landed. Reverting that commit as a quick rollback is an option if the adaptive change takes longer.

diego (ML): Also let's track quality — aggressive flushing can slightly increase jitter and packet overhead which may affect mobile clients. We'll include that in test matrix.

maya (Support): ACK. Marking this as in-progress. Will ping if Acme sees regression again. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident follow-up ticket created: INC-2026-287-streaming-flush (assigned to @jonas, @li, @diego, @maya)

jonas (Runtime): Closing loop: we'll leave the temporary config for 2h, then set more moderate threshold and kick off the adaptive flush RFC. Thanks for quick triage everyone.

maya (Support): thread note: root cause = runtime flush threshold change in v3.5.0. Mitigation = reduce threshold + force flush for streams, longer-term = adaptive flush based on token rate.
